1.1.evidence:
For the purposes of this law, the following notions mean: domestic violence – acts of physical, sexual, psychological, spiritual or economic violence, with the exception of actions of self-defense or defense of another person, including the threat of such acts, committed by a family member against another member of the same family, which caused material or moral harm to the victim; physical violence - intentional harm to bodily integrity or health through beating, pushing, throwing, hair pulling, pricking, cutting, burning, strangulation, biting, in any form and of any intensity, through poisoning, intoxication, other actions with similar effect; sexual violence - any violence of a sexual nature or any illegal sexual conduct within the family or in other interpersonal relationships, such as marital rape, prohibition of the use of contraceptive methods, sexual harassment; any unwanted, imposed sexual conduct; forced prostitution; any illegal sexual behavior in relation to a minor family member, including through caressing, kissing, posing of the child and through other unwanted touches of a sexual nature; other actions with similar effect; psychological violence – imposition of will or personal control; causing states of tension and psychological suffering through offenses, ridicule, abuse, insult, nicknaming, blackmail, demonstrative destruction of objects, verbal threats, ostentatious display of weapons or beating of domestic animals, neglect; interference in personal life; acts of jealousy; imposition of isolation through detention, including in the family home; isolation from family, community, friends; prohibition and/or creation of impediments in professional achievement or prohibition and/or creation of impediments in the completion of the educational program in the educational institution; persecution through contacting or attempting to contact by any means or through another person the victim who has been caused a state of anxiety, fear for their own safety or that of close relatives, being forced to modify their life conduct; dispossession of identity documents; intentional deprivation of access to information; other actions with similar effect; [Art.2 notion as worded by LP113 of 09.07.20, MO199-204/07.08.20 art.400; in force spiritual violence - underestimation or diminution of the importance of satisfying moral-spiritual needs through prohibition, limitation, ridicule, penalization of the aspirations of family members, through prohibition, limitation, ridicule or punishment of access to cultural, ethnic, linguistic or religious values; imposition of a personally unacceptable value system; other actions with similar effect or with similar repercussions; economic violence - deprivation of economic means, including deprivation of primary means of subsistence, such as food, medicines, basic necessities; abuse of various situations of superiority to steal the person's goods; prohibition of the right to own, use and dispose of common goods; inequitable control over common goods and resources; refusal to support the family; imposition of heavy and harmful work to the detriment of health, including of a minor family member; other actions with similar effect; violence against women – acts of gender-based violence that cause or may cause women physical, sexual or psychological suffering, including the threat of such acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, committed in the public or private sphere; [Art.2 notion introduced by LP113 of 09.07.20, MO199-204/07.08.20 art.400; in force adult victim – adult person who has been subjected to acts of domestic violence, in cohabitation; [Art.2 notion introduced by LP113 of 09.07.20, MO199-204/07.08.20 art.400; in force child victim – person who has not reached the age of 18 years, who has been subjected to or has witnessed acts of domestic violence, in cohabitation; [Art.2 notion introduced by LP113 of 09.07.20, MO199-204/07.08.20 art.400; in force moral harm – causing physical and/or psychological suffering, which leads to humiliation, fear, degradation, inability to defend against violence, feelings of frustration and other consequences of a similar nature; material harm - material damages, susceptible to financial/pecuniary evaluation or estimation, resulting from any act of domestic violence, in cohabitation, as well as the costs for the investigation of cases of domestic violence; aggressor - person who commits acts of domestic violence, in cohabitation. In case of complaints from several family members, with reciprocal accusations of committing acts of violence, the aggressor will be identified taking into consideration the following circumstances: which of the subjects involved acted in defense of themselves or another person; the probability of critical situations occurring for each person; the manner of action in the violence scene and the severity of injuries caused by each person; previous complaints of domestic violence, other circumstances that indicate the initiator of acts of violence; [Art.2 notion "victim" excluded by LP113 of 09.07.20, MO199-204/07.08.20 art.400; in force 07.09.20] protection order - legal act by which the court applies victim protection measures; crisis situation/critical situation – totality of circumstances that present imminent danger to the life and/or physical and/or mental integrity of the person, requiring urgent intervention with protective measures; emergency restriction order – administrative act issued by the police, through which protection measures are applied meant to ensure the immediate removal of the aggressor from the dwelling of the family subjected to violence and the establishment of prohibitions provided by law, in order to prevent the repetition/commission of acts of violence, thus guaranteeing the safety of the victim and other family members in their dwelling and outside it.
(4) The victim of domestic violence has the right to demand from the aggressor reparation, under the conditions of the law, of the material and moral damage caused by acts of violence, and from the state – reparation of material and moral damage as a result of failure to provide adequate assistance and protection.
